sections.what: Checks the code shape, makes sure the visitor is signed in, tries to join, and sends them to the crew. If joining fails for an expected reason, it shows a message asking for a new link.

summary: Handles an invite link: signs the visitor in if needed, joins the crew with the code, then opens the crew page.
purpose: Lets someone join a private crew from a link a friend shared.
why: The code comment states the flow: sign in first, then join and open the crew.
how: Reads the code and checks its shape, asks for the current user and sends them to sign in if needed, tries to join, then redirects to the crew on success or shows a friendly message on expected failures.
inputs: Invite code from the address and the signed-in user.
outputs: A redirect to sign-in, a redirect to the crew, or a page with an error message and a link back to crews.
risks: Only known domain errors are caught; anything else shows the general error page. The name joinOrOpen suggests it may do more than join, so the service must be checked before relying on that.
debug: If a valid link shows the error message, check joinCrewInput and joinOrOpen. If sign-in loops, check currentUserId and the login callback.
